newsitem.title: USA: Ford launches flexible fuel vehicle program.
newsitem.headline: Ford launches flexible fuel vehicle program.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Tuesday that over the next three to four years it plans to produce about 250,000 flexible fuel vehicles, which can run on gasoline, ethanol or any combination of the two fuels.
Ford said the use of E85 ethanol fuel, which is 85 percent ethanol and 15 percent gasoline, will improve performance while reducing exhaust emissions.
The automaker said its phased four-year program will bring more flexible fuel vehicles to market annually to match the growth of ethanol refueling stations around the United States.
Starting in fall 1998, Ford will equip 3.0-liter Ford Rangers with flexible fuel systems. The compact pickup will join the flexible fuel versions of its Taurus sedan.
The company said it will then offer other high-volume flexible fuel car and truck lines, including the Windstar mini-van, in subsequent years.

"We're announcing this four-year program to encourage the development and expansion of the ethanol infrastructure," Ross Roberts, Ford Motor vice president and general manager, Ford Division, said in a statement. "It does not make sense to dump a large number of FFVs (flexible fuel vehicles) on the market now when there are so few ethanol stations."
He said Ford believes announcing its product strategy and phasing in the flexible fuel vehicle introductions will help encourage the expansion of the infrastructure.

Upgraded components in flexible fuel vehicles include the fuel pump, fuel rails, fuel injectors, fuel lines and filler pipe. In addition, the package includes an electronic engine control module to calibrate engine response to different fuel mixtures of gasoline and ethanol, Ford said.
The Ford Taurus flexible fuel vehicle was introduced in 1992 and targeted at fleet customers.
Last year, Ford sold 5,272 FFV Tauruses (combined methanol/ethanol) and already has sold nearly as many in 1997.
Since enactment of the Clean Air Act of 1990, Ford said it has sold 12,117 flexible fuel vehicles -- more than half of the total of 23,232 sold by the auto industry.
